title: Chris Rumph II 1-on-1 interview after re-signing with Saints | 2026 Free Agency
text: I'm here with the recently re-signed Saints defensive end Chris Rumph. How are you? I'm great. How are you doing? I am good. When you were going through this process of free agency, how much did you want to land right back here with the Saints? Oh man, just going through this past season, um just being able to one second, I'm sorry. You're right. Uh just being able to go back and um think about what every what I've been through and being able to play 17 games, especially in a great city like New Orleans and the fans, I was excited to be back. Um I really grown into doing it not only for myself and my family, but for the city, especially with all the history that uh New Orleans has been through. Um so that was the main thing of me wanting to come back is being able to put put on for the city, honestly. What is it about the city and the fan base that resonated with you so quickly? Oh man, first of all, I'm from the South. Uh so I I felt back at home. Family was able to come to games and and hang out with me afterwards. Um and then I was able to just get that feel for Southern football again. Obviously, you know, nothing against the Chargers or whatever. I was over there in the West Coast, but y'all love football down here and I I do too. And and the fans here are amazing. I can't say enough about the fans, honestly. And um just seeing where this team was going at the end of the year and and seeing the hype and and the excitement around it. Obviously, you want to be a part of that. You mentioned that you played 17 games last season. That's the first time you've done that in your career, playing every single game. What was it about the way that you approached last year that led to that kind of success on the field? I think God God was just, you know, around me this year. He He blessed me with being able to be healthy. Um honestly, I didn't do anything different than what I've done in the past. Um but everything happens for a reason. Obviously, the injuries with bone you know, fractures and all that stuff, you can't control that, but you know, ever since I got those bone grafts in in my foot, everything's been good. So, um shout out to the the training staff as well as uh being on top of um everything that they do and giving me the resources you know, to stay healthy the whole year. Being reunited with a former coach over there with the Chargers and Brandon Staley here, you were able to really dive right in to what he wants to do here defensively. How do you see the scheme and what you guys are doing building for next year? Yeah, definitely building on what we uh put on tape this past year. Uh the physicality, being able to stop the run, but also rush the passer and and got have guys on the back end to cover the the speedy guys. And you know, with the the culture that we built um just the one season alone, it was very special and and you know, everybody was very close-knit together. Um you know, nobody was really arguing anything. Every time you know, you go in the building, it's you know, you're with the boys. And so I think that's something you don't take for granted. And then knowing that, you know, heading into free agency was definitely um something I took into consideration. You're always one of the personalities that we like to talk to because you're always in a good mood. You bring a lot of energy. Where does that come from? Uh my faith in Jesus, honestly, because uh without him I wouldn't be here. And and the things I've been through, um and I stay faithful. I I know that everything is going to work out in the end. So, I that's where I get I get it from because at the end of day, uh I'm just a servant. And you know, I've been put in position to where I can bless others, you know, and and spread that joy. Um and then you know, tell people where that comes from, just like you just did. So, I think that's uh that's what I I'm here to do. And uh obviously, you know, being able to use the abilities that he's blessed me with um to have a platform to do that. All right, speaking of the abilities, what are the goals for this upcoming season? You did a little special teams, a little defense last year. Yeah, I definitely got some goals, you know, uh special teams-wise, definitely all-pro. I I got to get all-pro. And then on defense, you know, at least I got to get at least five sacks and and help contribute to you know, a Super Bowl winning defense. Yeah, I mean Super Bowl sounds nice. I think I can get on board with that, for sure. Are you a NCAA March Madness person? Ah, so a lot of people, you know, first of all, shout out to my Duke Blue Devils, you know, good job, guys. You had me worried there for a second. Um but they came through, but you know, towards uh as I get older, I just a lot of things, you know, I got taxes, I got bills, I got all these things I got to do. Um but during this time, it's always fun to watch March Madness and sit down and you know, see guys um you know, live out their dreams. You never know who's going to win a game. I think that's the best part is there's no um there's no way for you to predict who's going to win the national championship. Every game is its own entity, its own life. And I think I enjoy that because it kind of translates a lot to you know, this the season. Um any given Sunday, I mean you got to show up and if you don't, you might get your butt kicked. I know, I had to ask because obviously, you went to Duke and they're the favorite this year, for sure. Are you coming back to New Orleans soon? What's one of the first things you're going to have to do? I'm going to Cafe Du Monde again. I'm going to get my beignets. I'm actually in Scottsdale, Arizona, so I've I've been missing that that that good old cooking down there, but um yeah, definitely going to Cafe Du Monde. Uh you know, going to locker room, you know, seeing, "Hey, you know, my locker is going to stay here this year." So, uh that'll be fun. Well, it's going to be great to have you back here. Look forward to whenever you do make the return and obviously, getting the season going, it's right around the corner. So, congratulations and welcome back. Thank you. I can't wait. Can't wait to be back.

title: Jaquan Brisker on becoming a Steeler, coming back home to Pittsburgh | 1-on-1 | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: What is it like just sitting here in the Steelers facility, a place that you did not grow up that far from? >> Yeah. Um I feel like um it's crazy, you know, to be here. It's amazing just to, you know, be, you know, in the presence of, you know, legends of, if you think about it, like the just the blueprint of everything, you know, the steel city, you know, what it means, you know, everything behind it. Um, I feel like it's a it's a surreal moment. Like I walked in here, I I got the chill, especially looking at the trophies. I mean, I seen too, but you know, just seeing the history, you know, of everything and, you know, the fans and what it means to the city, you know, the the city of champions and things like that, I feel like it's it's amazing. So, >> what did football mean to you growing up specifically in high school and as you furthered your career? >> Yeah, I feel like I started playing football around what, four or five years old and in Pittsburgh, you know, football's, you know, huge. You know, you look at, you know, the roots of it, you know, all the legends I passed through here. You look at the Hall of Famers, they really came from Pennsylvania and Pittsburgh. So, um, just being, you know, growing up there, just knowing, you know, how important football is and going to a powerhouse like Gateway, like you said, um, you know, just being around, you know, a lot of great athletes, you know, a lot of legends as pest doer and, you know, things like that. So, I feel like I mean, football, it meant a lot to me. >> Awesome. I want to show you something and you can just press play. Oh my gosh. Let's see what this kid is talking about. >> Jaquan Brisker. I play safety and receiver and I go to Gateway High School. >> We'll kick the ball and it's going to go high in the air and 2530 35 40 35 30 25 20 five touchdown. I describe my player as physical, athletic, and I can make plays when when my team needs me to make plays. I wear number three because my brother pass and he play I gay also and he had number three. So, I'm wearing number three for my brother. >> That's crazy. I need the ball back in my ass. >> My favorite music artist is Meek Mill. He's like a serious rapper and you know that he's the best. >> My favorite athlete would be Earl Thomas because he has a passion for a game. He takes the game serious and he flies around the ball. My favorite homemade meal would be my mom. >> My mom makes it. It's her recipe like and I like it. >> Yeah, that's so true. That's so true. >> My name is Jaquan Brisker and that's my blue chip spotlight. We'll have to get you a copy. >> I definitely do need that. That's hilarious. >> What do you think that kid in that video would be saying right now if he was sitting in this chair? >> Man, you know, being a a kid from the city of Pittsburgh. Um, and being in this position, you know, we're just blessed. We're just humbled. Um, you know, where we came from. um you know the the work we had to put in to get here and know to be in the hometown playing you know for the city you know in front of the fans you know for my family people like for the last name back in my jersey know it's it's crazy I feel like you know that kid you know he knew he had a future but he just didn't know how you know it would you know how it would continue so that's crazy >> you answered a lot of questions in there foods different things are all those still true >> yeah maybe not the favorite rapper part, but everything else is pretty much >> That's okay. That was high school. >> That was high school. Yeah. >> In terms of telling people that you were going to sign with the Steelers, who did you call first and what family members and friends got to know? >> My mom. My mom was the first one I called. I'm like, "Mom, I'm stealer." She like, "You sure, baby?" I'm like, "Yeah, I'm a stealer." She like, "Oh my gosh, I'm so excited." And then I had to tell my mom, had to tell my father, um had to tell, you know, my friends, um my brothers, you know, sisters, things like that. Really, my whole family. Um and everybody was just so excited. I was like, "This is meant to be." And I and I thought the same thing. I said, "It is meant to be, you know." Um I felt the love, you know, immediately and obviously um you know, grew up here and things like that. So, you know, I feel like it's going to be an amazing journey for sure. >> In terms of Joey Porter Jr., Did you tell him or did he somehow find out before? >> To be honest, he he was already ringing like, "What are you going to do? What are you going to do?" >> He was recruiting. >> Yeah, he was recruiting. So, I'm like, "I'm probably going to be a Steeler." And he, you know, kept calling. Then he called my agent. He's like, "What's going on?" So, when he called my agent, I'm like, "Oh, yeah. It's serious." So, like like I said, me and Joey talk all the time. So, um I'm Well, I called him on FaceTime. I'm like, "I'm about to be a Steeler for real." I'm like, "Let's go." I start sc like ah he's like let's go you know we were so excited. It was it was a great moment. So >> how cool would that be that you played in college together and now you're doing it at the next level. >> It's I mean it's amazing cuz in college um you know we were young but we were still you know great teammates but you know we performed on the field and then now you know we try to train with each other every year. So um just moving forward um being able to play with each other is is going to be amazing. like he obviously got older, he's more mature. Um we got a lot more swagger, things like that. Um and you know, we make plays and that's what the city needs. So, it's going to be amazing getting back with Joey and you know, I miss playing with him and I always told him we need to link up and now it's now it's here. So, it's going to be amazing. >> It's perfect. Last one for you. Uh what are you bringing to this team, to this defense? >> Yeah. Um I'll say leadership. um some swagger, passion, you know, um you know, care for the game and a lot of playmaking ability. Um just, you know, being around the football and helping my teammates elevate, you know, get better. Um you know, a lot of, you know, trash talking too, but that's okay. >> You know, things like that. Um just a lot of a lot of different things. And I feel like, you know, my teammates will love me for it. And, you know, once they, you know, feel my presence and, you know, once they start making plays, too, they going to see how happy I get for them. So once they just see what type of team I am, I feel like everybody's going to be happy. >> Well, welcome home. I don't get to say that often. >> Appreciate that. Thank you.
